scale_006:n1.prompt:
You are helping me reorganize our company's project-management workspace ({{vendor}}) into multiple teams, one per department. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) the list of departments/teams to create (names), (2) which members belong to each team, (3) whether any team should be a private sub-team restricted to specific members, and (4) who should get admin/edit vs view-only permissions on each team.

Once I provide this, do the following using {{vendor}}'s dashboard or API via my configured credentials:
1. Draft a proposed team structure showing each department team, its members, its permission roles (who can view/edit/admin), and any teams flagged as private sub-teams with restricted membership.
2. Check for naming conflicts with any existing teams and flag them.
3. Prepare the exact configuration you intend to apply for each team: team name, description, member list with roles, and privacy/visibility settings.
4. Do NOT create or modify any teams yet. Present the full draft plan to me as a clear checklist/table for review.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting this draft — do not create teams, assign members, or change permissions until I confirm.

Once I approve, create the teams exactly as approved, assign the specified members and roles, and configure any private sub-teams as restricted. After execution, report back with: the list of teams created, member/role assignments per team, which teams are private/restricted, and any errors or conflicts encountered during setup. If something in {{vendor}} prevents a requested configuration (e.g., a permission tier not available), flag it clearly rather than guessing a workaround.

scale_006:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure per-team workflow states in {{vendor}} as part of reorganizing into multiple teams. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the list of teams we've created in {{vendor}}, (2) each team's desired workflow stages (e.g., Backlog, Triage, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Done — or whatever variants each team wants), and (3) any team-specific naming or category mappings (start/unstarted/completed/canceled) they need.

Once I provide this, please:
1. For each team, review its current default workflow states in {{vendor}}'s team settings.
2. Draft a proposed workflow state configuration per team — listing state names, their category (backlog/unstarted/started/completed/canceled), and order — matching what I described.
3. Note any states that need to be added, renamed, reordered, or removed relative to the current default, and flag any that might break existing issues or automations if changed.
4. Compile all proposed per-team workflow configurations into a single clear summary document (team name, proposed states in order, category for each) so I can review everything at once before anything is changed in {{vendor}}.

Do not create, edit, or delete any workflow states in {{vendor}} yet — only prepare the draft configuration and the review summary. Since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, stop for human sign-off after presenting the draft summary, and wait for my explicit go-ahead on each team's configuration before making any changes.

When you report back, give me: the per-team draft workflow tables, any risks or conflicts you found with existing states/automations, and a clear list of open questions where my input is needed to finalize the configuration.

scale_006:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up cross-team projects in {{vendor}} as part of reorganizing our workspace into multiple teams. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} workspace/organization URL, (2) the list of teams that already exist in {{vendor}} (or should exist), (3) the names and goals of the cross-team initiatives/projects we need to create, (4) which team should be the 'owning team' for each project, and (5) any known cross-team dependencies (e.g., Project A in Team X depends on work in Team Y) that should be linked.

Using your configured credentials, access {{vendor}} and, for each initiative I describe:
- Draft a new project with a clear name and description reflecting the initiative's goal.
- Link the project to its owning team and any additional contributing teams.
- Set an initial status and priority for the project.
- Note any cross-team dependency relationships that should be tracked (which project/team depends on which), using {{vendor}}'s dependency or relation features.
- Prepare a roadmap-style summary showing each project, its owning team, linked teams, status, priority, and dependencies.

Do not create or save anything permanently yet — prepare all drafts as a proposed configuration. Compile a clear summary listing every project to be created, its owning team, linked teams, and dependency links, formatted so I can review it easily.

Since approval is required before changes are applied, present this full draft plan to me and stop for human sign-off. Do not create the projects, submit changes, or link teams in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve the plan. Once I confirm, let me know you're ready to proceed, but wait for my go-ahead before making any live changes.

scale_006:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up sprint cycles in {{vendor}} as part of reorganizing my engineering org into multiple teams. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the list of teams that now exist in {{vendor}} (or need to be created), (2) the desired sprint cadence (e.g., 1-week, 2-week) per team — they may differ, (3) the start day of the week for sprints, and (4) whether existing teams already have active cycles that need to be preserved or migrated.

Once I provide this, use your configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s API or admin interface and PREPARE the following for each team, without applying changes yet:
- A draft cycle/sprint configuration specifying cadence length, start day, and naming convention (e.g., 'Sprint 1', 'Sprint 2') for each team.
- A summary of how many upcoming cycles will be generated per team and their calculated start/end dates.
- Any cross-team alignment notes if I asked for synchronized sprint boundaries across teams (so roadmap and dependency views line up).
- A checklist confirming: teams exist, cadence settings match my input, no conflicting active cycles will be overwritten, and estimation/points settings (if applicable) are consistent with each team's existing workflow.

Do not create or activate any sprint cycles yet. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, so once your draft plan and checklist are ready, present them to me clearly (team name, cadence, start dates, cycle count) and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the full per-team cycle configuration you prepared, any assumptions you made due to missing info, and a clear note that you are awaiting my explicit approval before applying anything in {{vendor}}.

scale_006:n5.prompt:
You are helping me set up {{vendor}} channels for our newly reorganized teams as part of scaling into multiple teams in Linear/Jira. Goal: prepare a full plan for creating one dedicated {{vendor}} channel per team (plus any shared cross-team channel), and prepare the integrations that connect {{vendor}} to our project tool, but do not apply anything until I explicitly approve — a human must sign off before changes go live.

First, ask me for: (1) the final list of team names from our Linear/Jira reorg, (2) desired channel naming convention (e.g. team-<name>), (3) visibility (open vs private) for each channel, (4) which integration capabilities we want — installing a prebuilt {{vendor}} app from the marketplace, a custom slash command, an incoming webhook for automated notifications, or a richer interactive app with buttons/modals — and (5) my configured {{vendor}} credentials context (assume already configured, do not ask me to paste keys).

Then draft, but do not execute, the exact commands/configuration needed, for example the channel-creation command in the form: {{vendor}} channels create --name "<team-channel-name>" --type stream --visibility <open|private> for each team, plus a description of which integration type will be attached to each channel and how it maps to Linear/Jira team boards (e.g. webhook posts on issue status changes, slash command to create tickets).

Produce a clear checklist showing: channel name, visibility, linked team, and integration type for every team. Present this checklist to me for review and then stop for human sign-off — do not run any creation or integration commands until I confirm approval.

Goal: create a clear, shareable process doc describing how we are restructuring into multiple teams in our project management tool (team definitions, cross-team dependencies, roadmap views, and sprint cadences).

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available via my configured credentials: my {{vendor}} workspace/site details, the target parent page or workspace location for the new doc, the list of new teams and their leads/members, how cross-team dependencies should be tracked, which roadmap view(s) we're using, and our sprint cadence (length, start day, ceremonies).

Then draft the full page content: a title, an overview of why we're reorganizing, a section listing each new team with its scope and members, a section on cross-team dependency handling, a section describing roadmap view configuration, and a section on sprint cadence per team. Use {{vendor}}'s page creation API (create a new page — POST /v1/pages) to prepare this as a draft page in the location I specify, or lay it out clearly for me to paste in if API access isn't available.

Do not publish, share broadly, or link this page into any live navigation/roadmap yet — a human must explicitly approve before these changes are applied. Once the draft page is created (in draft/unpublished form if possible) or the content is fully prepared, stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft page link or full content, a summary of what's included, and a short checklist of decisions still needing my confirmation (team names, dependency process, cadence) before I approve and publish.
